original_question: Is Sfin(Omega,Omega) consistently additive (that is, can there be a model where finite or countable unions preserve this property as required by additivity)?
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact selection principle Sfin(Ω,Ω) and correctly recognizes that the paper asks a consistency question about whether this class can be additive.
missing_details: The paper's ambient objects are sets of real numbers (subspaces of R), not arbitrary topological spaces.
The statement should say 'consistent with ZFC' (or 'relative to ZFC'), since 'consistently' refers to existence of a model of ZFC where the closure property holds.
In the paper, 'additive' means preserved under finite unions only; countable unions correspond to the distinct notion of 'σ-additive'.
Sfin(Ω,Ω) should be defined explicitly: for every sequence of open ω-covers of X, one can choose finite subfamilies whose union is again an open ω-cover of X.
A cover in this context is nontrivial: X itself is not a member of the cover.
An ω-cover should be defined: every finite subset of the space is contained in some member of the cover.
The question is about the open-cover property Sfin(Ω,Ω), not the separate Borel analogue Sfin(BΩ,BΩ) in Problem 6.11.
The question is not about the later cardinal invariant add(J) ('the additivity number'); it asks only for closure under finite unions in some model.
For sets of reals, the paper notes that open covers may be assumed countable, but that is background rather than the main content of the problem.
refined_question: Is it consistent with ZFC that the class of sets of reals satisfying Sfin(Ω,Ω) is closed under finite unions? Equivalently: is there a model of ZFC in which, whenever X,Y ⊆ R each satisfy Sfin(Ω,Ω), then X ∪ Y also satisfies Sfin(Ω,Ω), where a set Z satisfies Sfin(Ω,Ω) if for every sequence (U_n)_{n∈N} of nontrivial open ω-covers of Z, there exist finite subfamilies F_n ⊆ U_n such that ⋃_{n∈N} F_n is again an open ω-cover of Z, and an ω-cover is an open cover such that every finite subset of Z is contained in some member of the cover?
justification: This is the nearest official formulation of your draft. In Section 6.4 ('Unions'), the paper first distinguishes additive (preserved under finite unions) from σ-additive (preserved under countable unions), and then asks exactly Problem 6.10: whether Sfin(Ω,Ω) is consistently additive. Section 1 supplies the definitions of Sfin(A,B), nontrivial covers, ω-covers, and Ω, and the introduction states that the chapter is restricted to sets of real numbers. Your draft therefore has the right target, but it needs the ZFC-consistency qualifier, the finite-union meaning of 'additive', and the underlying definitions to be fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper.
